title: fixedTimeLimit(d, unit): a timed-out attempt that ignores interrupts pins a non-daemon pool thread forever; each retry pins another and the JVM cannot exit
cause: The two-argument AttemptTimeLimiters.fixedTimeLimit creates new SimpleTimeLimiter(), i.e. a private Executors.newCachedThreadPool() (unbounded, non-daemon threads, no shutdown path, not reachable through the API). On timeout SimpleTimeLimiter.callWithTimeout only calls future.cancel(true), which sets the worker's interrupt flag but cannot stop a body that ignores interrupts, and Retryer.call immediately submits the next attempt, which the cached pool runs on a new thread because the old one is still busy.
trigger: A Retryer built with AttemptTimeLimiters.fixedTimeLimit(d, unit) and retryIfException()/retryIfRuntimeException() calls a callable that blocks in an operation that ignores Thread.interrupt() (a java.net.Socket read without SO_TIMEOUT against a peer that accepts but never answers, or entering a monitor held by a hung thread); every attempt times out.
consequence: Each timed-out attempt permanently pins one non-daemon pool thread: one call() with 2 attempts leaves 2 stuck threads; call() can return 42 while attempt 1 still runs; under the default neverStop the pinned threads grow linearly (100 after 5 s at a 50 ms limit) until thread creation fails and call() throws ExecutionException(OutOfMemoryError: unable to create native thread); after main() returns the JVM does not exit (still alive 95 s later, beyond the 60 s keep-alive behind issue #92).
premises: The callable is arbitrary user code that may block in an operation that ignores Thread.interrupt() (classic socket read without timeout, monitor entry, swallowed InterruptedException).

Built and run against Guava 22.0: SimpleTimeLimiter() delegates to Executors.newCachedThreadPool() (SimpleTimeLimiter.java:81-84) and callWithTimeout reacts to a timeout only with future.cancel(true) (SimpleTimeLimiter.java:164-166).
JDK Executors.newCachedThreadPool() creates non-daemon threads with an unbounded maximum pool size; its 60 s keep-alive reaps only idle threads.

Timeouts are retried only when the rejection predicate accepts UncheckedTimeoutException (retryIfException/retryIfRuntimeException); without that each call() pins at most one thread, but repeated calls still accumulate pinned threads.
Scope is the 2-argument fixedTimeLimit overload; with the 3-argument overload a user-supplied daemon pool avoids the JVM-exit hang but not the per-attempt thread growth.
